title: Textures preserved across boolean operations
description: 'Textures should be maintained across boolean ops.' Pass the CRAW-3 UV coordinates (and a material index) into Manifold as vertex properties (MeshGL64 numProp channels) so Manifold interpolates them at intersection vertices, then rebuild the UV slot on the result and use CRAW-13 provenance to assign each output face its origin's MaterialData. The result bundle keeps one material per origin (a multi-material slot) so the merged crawfish renders both scans' photographic textures. Seam vertices shared by faces of different origins keep per-face material; if a per-corner UV representation is required for that, introduce it here (see CRAW-3 unknown).
definition-of-done: 1. mesh_boolean on two textured cubes yields a bundle whose every face has UVs and a material index; the checker pattern is continuous across the intersection seam in a screenshot. 2. Union of two crawfish scans renders each region with its own scan texture. 3. UV interpolation error at intersection vertices is below 1e-4 in a unit test with analytically known UVs (planar quads). 4. Slots absent on inputs -> result has no slots, no exception. 5. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: two planar-UV cubes, union; verify UV at a known intersection point equals the analytic value. 2. Unit: mixed inputs (one textured, one not) produce a result with material index -1 for untextured faces. 3. run-scene mesh-boolean with a textured cube_boolean variant; screenshot.
unknowns: Whether to bake both scan textures into one atlas later for export (CRAW-20) or keep multi-material
changes-made: UVs ride through Manifold as interpolated vertex properties. ManifoldProvenanceBindings gained manifold_meshgl64 (the numProp constructor the vendored ManifoldBindings hardcodes to 3), manifold_meshgl64_merge, manifold_of_meshgl64 and manifold_meshgl64_num_prop; importProperties() builds a solid with 5 channels (x,y,z,u,v), merging first so vertices split by UV weld back instead of reading as a crack.

ManifoldMeshExport now carries propertiesPerVertex (read from manifold_meshgl64_num_prop) and strides by it; its vertexPositions field became vertexProperties and cornerCoordinate() takes a channel, so the CRAW-13 provenance path reads positions unchanged whatever the channel count.

New BooleanVertexProperties builds one operand's kernel vertex table: positions only at 3 channels, or positions plus UV with one vertex per distinct corner UV (chained dedup, bit-exact compare) at 5. QuadTriangulation.build(CornerUvField) carries per-corner UVs onto the triangles, which only an already-triangular operand can do (a corner field is indexed three per face, so a split quad has no corner to read); it logs and drops otherwise.

Unknown 1 answered: Manifold does interpolate vertex properties across a boolean, linearly, and does keep property discontinuities. With UVs affine in position on two unit cubes, every corner of the union reproduces the analytic UV within 1e-4 (the test asserts that bound; the observed error is float round-trip only). Seams survive because a MeshGL vertex is a property vertex and the merge vectors say which ones are one point.

MeshBooleanResult gained cornerU/cornerV per output face corner. The backend welds the output by exact position when properties split it (VertexPositionIndex, the CRAW-13 class), so a UV seam no longer cracks the result mesh; the per-corner UV field carries the seam instead. Untextured booleans keep their old vertex numbering untouched, so MESH-50 is unaffected either way.

New MaterialSet slot (_materials plus per-face _face_material IntField, NO_MATERIAL = -1) is the multi-material carrier; MaterialData._material stays the single-material one. mesh_boolean gives each output face the material of the input face it was copied or cut from, looked up through the CRAW-13 faceSourceOperand/faceSourceQuad pair, so operands that are themselves multi-material compose. The node now drops the stale _uv/_material/_materials/_face_material slots it used to carry over from operand A.

Scaffolding and demos (previous agent, recorded now): CheckerMaterialNode (checker_material) triangulates a mesh and gives it world-space box UVs plus a generated two-tone checker texture; cube_boolean_textured.dsl unions two checker cubes; MeshBooleanTexturedScene (id mesh-boolean-textured) renders it with the textured draw; crawfish_union.dsl unions IMG_4109 and IMG_4110 (repaired, the second nudged 0.25 along X). HalfEdgeMeshRuntime uploads one base-colour texture per material and draws one index range per material, faces naming none falling back to the solid colour; CornerUvSplit takes a face order so those ranges are contiguous.

Hole-fill triangles: repair_mesh leaves NaN UVs on the triangles it fills holes with, and Manifold rejects a non-finite property (NON_FINITE_VERTEX), so the crawfish union failed. BooleanVertexProperties now hands the kernel a finite stand-in (MISSING_UV_STAND_IN) for those corners, and the backend puts NaN back on every output face whose provenance source face had no UVs, including every face from an untextured operand.

Seam weld by merge vectors: the backend welded output property vertices by exact position, which also fused the distinct copies repair_mesh splits a pinched vertex into and failed on the crawfish with 'Non-manifold or duplicate face edge'. It now welds by the output MeshGL's mergeFromVert/mergeToVert (ManifoldProvenanceBindings binds manifold_meshgl64_merge_length/_from_vert/_to_vert; ManifoldMeshExport carries them). Untextured booleans still skip the weld, so their vertex numbering is unchanged.

mesh_boolean drops operand A's _edge_marks slot, which indexes edges the result no longer has; carried through, it made the mesh viewer switch to the STAGES shader and hide the texture. Both of MeshNodeViewerScene's DSL routes (the resource reload and the -Dixdar.model=<file>.dsl path) now upload the graph's whole bundle through one uploadGraphOutput helper, so a textured graph output draws textured. The QuadTriangulation dropped-UV log line and a textured-draw log line in MeshBooleanScene were removed as scaffolding.

Verification: BooleanTextureTransferTest (7 procedural tests: analytic UV at cut vertices within 1e-4, box-projected UV seams weld into a closed mesh keeping each face's projection, every face has UV + material, untextured operand faces get NO_MATERIAL and NaN UVs, NaN hole-fill UVs survive the kernel and stay NaN only on their faces, no slots in -> no slots out, stale slots including _edge_marks dropped). Screenshots tmp/craw-14-textured-cubes.png (checker continuous across the cut) and tmp/craw-14-crawfish-union*.png (each scan region in its own texture). Launch entries 'CRAW-14: mesh-boolean-textured', 'CRAW-14: crawfish-union' and the permanent 'Mesh Boolean Textured'.
